headline: DISCOVERY MINING DSV: BORDEN MAIN ZONE EXTENDS 500m+ DOWN-PLUNGE NE — 9.16 g/t Au OVER 25.9m, RESOURCE ESTIMATE DUE LATE 2026
snippet: Discovery Mining Ltd. (TSX: DSV) released results from 21 holes (7,036 metres) at its operating Borden Mine in Ontario's Abitibi region on August 10, 2026, confirming the Main Zone now extends more than half a kilometre further down-plunge to the northeast than previously known — with the zone remaining open. The headline underground intercept returned 9.16 g/t gold over 25.9 metres including high-grade sections grading 18.40 g/t. Surface drilling confirmed the northeast extension at depth as part of the company's 255,000–285,000 metre 2026 exploration program across a 1,000 km² Abitibi land position. A formal resource estimate for the Dome and TVZ deposits is on track for late 2026, setting up a potential resource rerate at current gold prices above $4,300 per ounce.

headline: UR-ENERGY Q2 2026: U.S. LARGEST ISR PRODUCER PACKAGES 140,873 LBS U3O8 — SHIRLEY BASIN CLEARED FOR FULL PRODUCTION
snippet: Ur-Energy Inc. (NASDAQ: URG) reported Q2 2026 results on August 10, 2026, posting its strongest-ever drumming quarter: 140,873 lbs of U3O8 packaged — up 47.4% over Q1 2026 and 25.7% over Q2 2025 — and 149,747 lbs shipped to the conversion facility, up 44% quarter-over-quarter. The strategic milestone is the final state regulatory authorization received in late June 2026 to begin full production operations at Shirley Basin, which captured 10,634 lbs while running only limited operations during Q2. With Lost Creek ramping and Shirley Basin now fully authorized, Ur-Energy describes itself as both the largest and fastest-growing ISR uranium producer in the United States — a position that matters as utility term contracts price at $94/lb versus spot at $86.50/lb, reflecting structural supply urgency from utilities and AI data centre operators competing for long-term nuclear capacity.

headline: MP MATERIALS SURGES 23.5% W/W ON +89% Q2 REVENUE BEAT — USAR +29%, UUUU +24% ON U.S. POLICY BETS
snippet: MP Materials Corp. (NYSE: MP) stock extended gains on Monday August 10, 2026 — up 6.76% on the day after rallying 23.54% over the prior week — following a Q2 FY26 report posting $108.49 million in revenue, up 89% year-over-year and beating consensus by 13%. The company produced 840 metric tonnes of NdPr oxide (up 41% year-over-year) and sold more than 1,006 metric tonnes, more than double the prior-year volume. The rally pulled the entire domestic rare earth complex higher: USA Rare Earth (USAR) gained 29% and Energy Fuels (UUUU) added 24% on the week, as investors priced in accelerating U.S. policy support following Trump's White House mining summit and the Executive Order barring Chinese-origin critical minerals from U.S. defence procurement effective January 2027.

headline: GOLD $4,329, SILVER $63.80 PRE-CPI: BULLS WATCHING $4,300 SUPPORT AS TUESDAY INFLATION PRINT SETS NEXT $200 MOVE
snippet: Gold and silver held near recent highs on August 10, 2026 — gold at $4,329.20 and silver at $63.80 — as markets paused the payrolls-driven advance to position for Tuesday's July CPI data. Consensus expects +3.4% year-on-year headline inflation and +2.5% core; a soft reading consistent with the July payrolls miss (−23,000 vs. +180,000 consensus) would validate the dovish Fed narrative and open a path toward $4,481–$4,500 resistance, while a hot print — crude oil up 23.5% over the prior month — could test whether $4,300 holds as support. Markets have shifted odds of a September Fed rate hike to approximately 44% from near two-thirds a week prior. PPI and retail sales data are also due this week, making it the most macro-dense week for precious metals since the January 2026 all-time high run.

headline: PBOC ADDS 20 TONNES IN JULY — 21ST CONSECUTIVE MONTH, BIGGEST SINGLE PURCHASE SINCE OCTOBER 2023
snippet: China's People's Bank of China increased its official gold reserves by approximately 20 metric tonnes (640,000 ounces) in July 2026 — the largest single-month addition since October 2023 and the 21st consecutive month of accumulation — pushing total holdings above 76 million ounces. June had seen a more modest 15-tonne addition. China's gold holdings remain below 10% of total foreign exchange reserves, leaving substantial room for continued rebalancing, and the PBOC has consistently bought on price dips, including during the June–July gold correction. The trend confirms China as a structural, price-insensitive buyer executing a long-term reserve diversification strategy — a persistent demand floor that gold analysts now treat as a defining feature of the 2024–2026 gold bull market.

headline: TRUMP MINES THE SUMMIT: $2B+ IN DEALS AS RIO TINTO, BHP, FREEPORT ANSWER WHITE HOUSE CALL ON CRITICAL MINERALS
snippet: President Trump convened executives from Rio Tinto, BHP, Freeport-McMoRan, MP Materials, USA Rare Earth, Energy Fuels, and The Metals Company at the White House on August 8, 2026, announcing more than $2 billion in fresh financing commitments for critical mineral and mining projects — including a $1.4 billion conditional Department of War loan to silicon-carbon anode maker Sila Nanotechnologies and $400 million for Australia's Sunrise Energy Metals to build a full scandium value chain. The White House said it has now signed or approved 160 minerals deals worth approximately $40 billion since January 2025. The summit was framed as a direct counter to China's critical mineral export restriction regime, and officials signalled more deals are coming. The meeting follows an Executive Order signed July 20 barring Chinese-origin critical minerals from U.S. defence procurement effective January 1, 2027.

headline: BIG GOLD-STOCK BREAKOUT: GDXJ SURGES FROM FALLING WEDGE — HAMILTON ARGUES MINERS POSITIONED FOR NEW RECORD HIGHS
source_name: Adam Hamilton / Ahead of the Herd (syndicated GoldSeek)
snippet: Analyst Adam Hamilton documents the gold stock sector's decisive upside breakout from a multi-month falling wedge, recording GDXJ's 7.4% single-session surge through major resistance — a pattern breakout that Hamilton argues resolves upward roughly 90% of the time after this duration of compression. The analysis contextualises the move within gold miners' near-record Q2 2026 earnings cycle: with gold prices 70% higher year-over-year, the GDX top 25 are on track for their second-best earnings quarter ever, and GDXJ mid-tiers are posting implied unit profits of approximately $2,850 per ounce. Hamilton frames GDX and GDXJ as both technically confirmed and fundamentally undervalued relative to the gold price, with current P/Es in low-to-mid teens despite record sector profits — the same setup that preceded the major 2020 and 2016 gold stock bull runs.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $14,000/TONNE AS COMEX HITS RECORD 650K TONNES — REFINED COPPER TARIFF DECISION NOW WITH TRUMP
snippet: Copper is trading near $14,000 per tonne as U.S. COMEX copper inventories have surged to a record 650,000 tonnes — the largest U.S. copper stockpile since records began — as traders front-loaded imports ahead of a presidential decision on whether to impose a phased 15% (from January 1, 2027) rising to 30% (from January 1, 2028) tariff on refined copper imports. The Secretary of Commerce submitted the June 30, 2026 deadline assessment on domestic copper markets to the President; the timing and form of any tariff proclamation is now a presidential call. Copper has risen approximately 49% year-over-year. The tariff premium is estimated at $1,000–$2,000 per tonne above global LME fundamentals. For junior copper developers in North America — Arizona, British Columbia, Nevada, Ontario — a final tariff regime represents the most powerful price tailwind for domestic production in decades.

headline: RARE EARTH PRICES PULL BACK IN AUGUST 2026 AFTER JULY RALLY — ERBIUM BUCKS TREND AS MOST OXIDES CONSOLIDATE
snippet: Rare earth oxide prices entered a consolidation phase in August 2026 following July's rally, with most elements seeing modest pullbacks from monthly highs as Chinese domestic demand and quota-constrained supply create a sideways-to-softer short-term pricing environment. Erbium is the notable exception, with specific demand from the fiber optics and medical laser sectors sustaining a bid. The pullback follows China's Bayan Obo 50% ore capacity expansion announcement and Malaysia's signals of a possible partial easing of its 2024 raw rare earth export moratorium — both of which added supply-side uncertainty. For Western junior rare earth developers, the price consolidation is a headline risk but not a structural reversal: the U.S. Executive Order barring Chinese-origin REEs from defence procurement effective January 2027 and the Trump administration's escalating financing commitments to domestic producers remain the demand-pull signals underwriting project economics.

headline: BRS RESOURCES BRS.CSE: FIRST ASSAYS CONFIRM Au-Ag-Cu AT SILVERGOLD MOUNTAIN IN MULATOS GOLD BELT, SONORA
source_name: Junior Mining Network / BRS Resources Ltd. (CSE: BRS)
snippet: BRS Resources Ltd. (CSE: BRS) released initial rock sample assay results on August 10, 2026 from a 16-sample surface program at its SilverGold Mountain Project in the Mulatos Gold Belt, Sonora, Mexico — one of North America's most productive high-sulfidation epithermal corridors (hosting the Alamos Gold Mulatos mine). Results returned values up to 2.06 g/t gold and 76.3 g/t silver alongside copper grades up to 1.20% Cu, confirming polymetallic mineralization signatures consistent with the district-defining vein system. These are surface rock chip samples, not drill intercepts — the next material milestone is a drill program — but surface sample grades in the Mulatos district have historically correlated with high-grade epithermal vein systems at depth. The company has also recently signed a definitive agreement to expand its Sonora concession footprint.
